![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14131939/assets/1253965689fbeb233ca3eda553cca8ea8bced9feb81ebc6565c9b65782066b47.png)

Suppose that $F$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ defined over the region $D$ above. Given that 

$$
{∮}_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r=2,\,{∮}_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r=9,\,{∮}_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r=8,
$$

where ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ are oriented counterclockwise and ${C}_{3}$ is oriented clockwise, calculate the value of ${∮}_{∂D}F\cdot \text{d}r.$
question.worked_solution:
To calculate the total circulation of a vector field over the boundary of a region containing holes, we add together the circulations over each *positively oriented* boundary.

Remember that:

- the positive direction is *counterclockwise* for the *outer* curve ${C}_{1}$ (because the region $D$ is always on the left as we traverse ${C}_{1}$ counterclockwise), and

- the positive direction is *clockwise* for the *inner* curves ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ (because the region $D$ is always on the left as we traverse ${C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ clockwise).

The diagram below shows the positive orientations of all three curves.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14131939/assets/cad0f92fdd888243562619b410a200ca040ca43f83bfd15fb124c8a8ecae4df6.png)

Notice that the positive orientation of the inner curve ${C}_{2}$ is opposite that of ${C}_{2}$ as stated in the question.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{∂D}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={∮}_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{∮}_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{∮}_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =2-9+8 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
